name: Ja'ir (Son of Manasseh, captured villages in Gilead)
title: Conqueror of the Villages of Gilead
summary: Ja'ir was a descendant of Manasseh, Joseph's son, through Manasseh's grandson Machir. He is known for capturing several villages in the Gilead region east of the Jordan during the conquest of Canaan, and these villages were called Havvoth-Jair (the tent-villages of Ja'ir). His conquests were an important part of Israel's settlement in Transjordan.

keyEvents.title: The Conquest of the Villages in Gilead
keyEvents.description: Ja'ir, who belonged to the tribe of Manasseh, went out and captured the villages in Gilead and called them Havvoth-Jair (the villages of Ja'ir).

keyEvents.title: Allocation of the Gilead Region
keyEvents.description: As part of the distribution of the land east of the Jordan, Ja'ir's descendants received their portion in Gilead and Bashan, in accordance with Moses' allocations.

keyEvents.title: Ja'ir's Villages Mentioned in the Book of Joshua
keyEvents.description: Havvoth-Jair, the sixty cities in the Gilead region, were confirmed as part of the inheritance of the half-tribe of Manasseh during the land distribution after the conquest.

keyEvents.title: Jair's Lineage through Hezron and Machir
keyEvents.description: First Chronicles describes Jair's ancestry: his father Segub was the son of Hezron from the tribe of Judah, who married the daughter of Machir, linking Jair to both Judah and Manasseh.

keyEvents.title: Solomon's Administration of Havvoth-Jair
keyEvents.description: During King Solomon's reign, Havvoth-Jair continued to be regarded as an important district with its own administrator, demonstrating the lasting significance of Jair's conquests.
